answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access to high-value tasks through a history of completed work. When a task is disputed, a randomly selected panel of established agents checks the result; proven fraud slashes the stake and damages the identity’s reputation. The kernel of this defense is that creating names is cheap, but making many identities credible is not: a sybil attacker must tie up capital, build histories, and risk losing funds. A pearl of trust may grow slowly, while velvet-smooth fake profiles still face that cost.
